messages:
olivia: Heads-up — ~180 GPU pods in us-west-2 got evicted over the last 10m. Kubelet failing readiness for several sidecars because DNS lookups to internal service IPs keep timing out.

sam: Same here, saw the alerts. kubelet logs show `dial udp 10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout` coming from readiness probes. CoreDNS dashboards: tail latency spike and a bunch of SERVFAILs.

diego: Any east-west packet loss or MTU churn? I captured pings between az-a and az-b earlier and saw ~1.2% loss and a few fragmented UDP retransmits.

maya: We rolled an MTU clamp change on nodepool-gpu yesterday at 03:20 UTC as part of egress tuning. Rolling back that change now to rule it out.

ops-oncall: oncall — temporary mitigation suggestion: increase readiness probe period to 60s for the gpu pods and set failureThreshold to 6 so we avoid immediate evictions while we investigate. Also consider pausing autoscaler.

olivia: paste kubelet logs and a failing probe sample:
```
Mar 04 08:41:02 kubelet[1234]: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.1.123.45:8080/ready": dial udp 10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout
Mar 04 08:41:02 kubelet[1234]: Pod gpu-job-42 evicted: Readiness probe failure
```

sam: Quick dig from a node in the same AZ: `dig +time=2 +tries=2 gpu-api.svc.cluster.local @10.0.0.10`
Result: `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` or occasionally `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, rcode: SERVFAIL`.

diego: Can someone run conntrack snapshot and CoreDNS logs? If conntrack is saturated we get dropped UDP, causing retransmits and timeouts. Example check: `conntrack -S` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l`. Also confirm kube-proxy mode and iptables conntrack timeouts.

maya: Rolling back MTU clamp now and bringing nodepool-gpu back to previous config. Also increasing node-local-dns cache size and replicas in us-west-2 as an interim.

sam: Seeing fewer failures after node-local-dns scale-up but not gone. CoreDNS still shows high request duration for certain pod IP ranges.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1754 — title: "us-west-2 GPU pod evictions due to DNS timeouts" — assigned: eng-infra.

sre-jen: Noting prior incident pattern: MTU clamps + RDMA NICs caused UDP fragment drops on our RDMA-enabled instances. If RDMA NICs drop fragments, small UDP DNS packets can be lost even if TCP is fine. Check `ethtool -S <iface>` for rx_errors and `dmesg` for NIC warnings. Also check if any iptables DROP rules were added during yesterday's maintenance.

olivia: Quick mitigation deployed: bumped node-local-dns cache to 1500, added 2 more node-local instances (AZ-local), applied pod affinity so gpu pods prefer DNS replicas in same AZ, extended readiness probes per ops suggestion. Monitoring now.

sam: +1 on affinity. We should also add a server fallback in CoreDNS for the node-local->coredns hop to avoid a single overloaded forwarder.

diego: I captured tcpdump around a failing probe: lots of DNS retries from the pod, then a burst of retransmits to the same upstream IP and then a conntrack drop counter tick. Will attach packet capture to the incident.

maya: Rollback complete on MTU clamp. No new evictions in the last 6m. Keeping mitigations in place for 30m window.

ops-oncall: I'll hold autoscaler and any disruptive nodepool changes until postmortem. If things stay green for 30m, file a postmortem and propose these action items: revert MTU change permanently until RDMA/frag tests, increase default node-local cache for gpu nodepools, add conntrack capacity test in Chaos harness. :thumbsup:

olivia: Good plan. If stable after 30m I'll open the postmortem and assign owners. Thanks everybody for the quick responses.

sre-jen: Addendum — recommend a follow-up: run RDMA/MTU frag test matrix on a staging GPU pool (vary MTU 1500/8900, simulate small UDP bursts) before reapplying any cluster-wide MTU tuning.

sam: copying packet captures into INC-2026-1754.

olivia: monitoring shows internal DNS error rate dropped 80% after fixes. Keeping thread open until the postmortem. :eyes:
